title: Kingdom of Majorca
capsule: The Kingdom of Majorca was created in 1276 when James I of Aragon's testament bequeathed the Balearic Islands, the counties of Roussillon and Cerdanya, and the lordship of Montpellier to his younger son James II, who was simultaneously required by the Treaty of Perpignan in 1279 to hold these territories as an Aragonese vassal. The realm functioned as a significant western Mediterranean commercial power under James II and his son Sancho, but was progressively weakened by Aragonese political pressure. Peter IV of Aragon invaded in 1343–1344 and the last Majorcan king, James III, was killed at the Battle of Llucmajor on 25 October 1349, extinguishing the dynasty and absorbing the kingdom into the Crown of Aragon.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The kingdom's core Balearic territory is well attested; the continental possessions in Roussillon, Cerdanya, and Montpellier involved complex feudal jurisdictions that complicate cartographic representation of a unified realm.
